Update: Steaming

By: Laura Byrne | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We revisit the steam enthusiasts at Friends of the Rail

Unique Selling Point:
Steam train travel brings back the romance of yesteryear. But this old-fashioned pastime faces a very modern problem: scrap metal theft.

Summary:
Last year, we travelled with Friends of the Rail on a lovingly restored steam train between Hermanstad and Rayton, where our journey was cut short by the removal of 240m of railway line by scrap metal thieves. After a long 10 month negotiation process, the missing rail has finally been replaced and the stately steam train can complete her journey to historic Cullinan once more.

Script:


Travel by steam train brings back the nostalgia and romance of yesteryear.
UPSOUND (CB 2017): Mom: “He’s loving it, he’s obsessed with trains. We’ve been talking about it for a month.
In July last year, we travelled with Friends of the Rail on a lovingly restored steam train between Hermanstad and Cullinan.
UPSOUND (CB 2017): Les Labuschagne: “The fact that the technology, you know, is 70, 80 100 years old, and to be able to take yourself back all those years that what it really is.
But this historic pastime is plagued by a modern problem: scrap metal theft. Driver Les Labuschagne was on board when a train derailed in March 2017: thieves had carried off 240m of line overnight.
UPSOUND: Les Labuschagne: So since then we were only running trains up until Rayton. And then ferrying the passengers by bus from Rayton to Cullinan.
The theft was more than a mood killer: it financially crippled Friends of the Rail.
UPSOUND: Les Labuschagne: We’ve had to cease all projects here at our site here in Hermanstad. All restorations, all repairs, payment plans had to be made, etc etc. So it impacted us very heavily.
But after 10 months of negotiations, Transnet’s heritage division and branch line management replaced the rail and the line was reopened this month.
UPSOUND: Les Labuschagne: We fortunately have now a system whereby we patrol the line daily. We have also got the assistance of Transnet’s security transport that also patrol the line.
Friends of the Rail now have big plans for the future, starting with restoration of some of the stately old ladies waiting patiently in the yard.
UPSOUND: Les Labuschagne: I believe that there is a very big market, tourism market, for heritage trains and steam in South Africa. It’s very romantic it’s the old, it’s the nostalgia of it. It’s wonderful.
